ideas.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge
ideas.description: Expose cells to a defined, transient AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or injury signal), let AP-1 activity return to baseline, then re-stimulate days to weeks later. Compare transcriptional output (RNA-seq, nascent RNA) and kinetics against naive cells to test for primed or enhanced responses.

ideas.title: Time-resolved chromatin accessibility and AP-1 occupancy
ideas.description: Run ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag/ChIP-seq for FOS/JUN family members, and H3K27ac/H3K4me1 profiling before, during, and long after stimulation. Test whether AP-1-dependent enhancers remain open or poised after AP-1 binding disappears, indicating a persistent epigenetic trace.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 perturbation to test necessity and sufficiency
ideas.description: Use dominant-negative FOS (A-FOS), degron-tagged JUN/FOS, or CRISPRi/KO to remove AP-1 at different times, and optogenetic or inducible expression to pulse it. Determine whether AP-1 is needed only to establish the memory, or also to maintain it, and whether a pulse alone is sufficient to create it.

ideas.title: Single-cell live imaging and multiome tracking of lineages
ideas.description: Use live reporters of AP-1 activity (e.g., FOS-GFP or AP-1 response element reporters) with lineage tracing, plus single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) over time. Quantify whether the memory persists through cell divisions, how heterogeneous it is, and whether prior AP-1 dynamics (amplitude, duration, pulsing) predict later responses.

ideas.title: Locus-specific causal editing of AP-1 motifs and chromatin state
ideas.description: Mutate or delete AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers, or recruit dCas9 effectors (writers/erasers of H3K27ac or DNA methylation) to them. Measure whether the primed state, and the enhanced re-response of nearby genes, depends on those sites and on partner pioneer factors or chromatin remodelers, such as SWI/SNF.
